statement: Summaries of NASA combustion investigations relevant to fire safety. Every field comes from the NASA source named with it; quotes are copied exactly and are under 15 words. Fields marked 'Not yet summarised' were not found in the sources we checked.

flags.solid_materials: Flammability of solid materials such as fabrics and plastics (fire prevention through material selection)
flags.ventilation_flow: Effect of air flow speed, which matters in microgravity cabins
flags.habitat_atmosphere: Tests at oxygen levels or pressures beyond Earth air, relevant to exploration habitats and suits
flags.partial_gravity: Lunar or Mars gravity, or a method that mimics or assesses it
flags.large_scale: Fires larger than small laboratory samples

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigations.hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), using a slightly modified SPICE flow duct
investigations.status: Archived by NASA Glenn (BASS operations started in March 2012)
investigations.objective: Examines how a wide variety of solid fuel samples burn and go out in microgravity, with air flow speed as the main variable, and applies nitrogen as a suppressant to selected flames.
investigations.fuels: 41 fuel samples in three categories: flat samples, solid spheres and candles within tubes. Thin flat samples include the SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, Nomex and Ultem; thick samples include PMMA.
investigations.conditions: ISS air, nominally 21% oxygen at one atmosphere; nitrogen was used for tests as low as 17% oxygen. In one fabric test the flow was stepped down from 10 cm/s to below 1 cm/s.
investigations.variables: Air flow speed (main variable), sample type and size, oxygen concentration, nitrogen suppressant
investigations.measurements: Concurrent-flow spread rate and limiting flame length (thin samples); flame growth rate, flame-to-fuel distance and solid regression rate from high-resolution images

flags.solid_materials: Burns a wide variety of solid fuel samples, including spacecraft fabrics and plastics
flags.ventilation_flow: The air flow speed is the main variable
flags.suppression: A nitrogen suppressant was applied to selected flames

quotes.text: burning and extinction characteristics of a wide variety of fuel samples in microgravity
materials in microgravity, with adequate ventilation, burn as well if not better

investigations.earth_application: BASS results contribute to computational models used in the design of fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth.

o2_range.label: 17% to 21% O2 (ISS air; nitrogen used to go as low as 17%)

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration
investigations.platform: Cygnus cargo vehicle, after it leaves the ISS
investigations.hardware: Flow duct and avionics bay inside an enclosure about 0.5 m wide, 1 m deep and 1.3 m long (Saffire-I)
investigations.status: Saffire-I completed July 2016; Saffire-II completed 27 Nov 2016; Saffire-III launched 18 Apr 2017; Saffire-IV ignited 11 May 2020; Saffire-V and -VI followed
investigations.objective: Studies large-scale flame growth and material flammability limits in space by burning samples inside a Cygnus cargo vehicle after it has left the space station and before its destructive reentry.
investigations.fuels: Saffire-I: a cotton-fiberglass blend sample 0.4 m wide by 1 m long. Saffire-II: nine samples including cotton-fiberglass, Nomex and the acrylic glass used for spacecraft windows. Saffire-IV: SIBAL cloth (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass) and the Saffire-II materials.
investigations.conditions: Saffire-III burned the Saffire-I fabric at a higher flow velocity. Saffire-IV burned the Saffire-II materials at different pressures and oxygen levels. Saffire-V examines the range of pressures and oxygen concentrations expected in future exploration spacecraft.
investigations.variables: Sample material, flow velocity, pressure and oxygen concentration
investigations.measurements: Not yet summarised

flags.solid_materials: Burns spacecraft materials such as cotton-fiberglass fabric, Nomex and window acrylic
flags.large_scale: Saffire-I's sample was 0.4 m by 1 m; before it, the largest space fire experiment was about the size of an index card
flags.ventilation_flow: Saffire-III repeated the Saffire-I fabric at a higher flow velocity
flags.habitat_atmosphere: Saffire-V examines pressures and oxygen concentrations expected in future exploration spacecraft

quotes.text: investigate large-scale flame growth and material flammability limits in space

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
investigations.hardware: An insert for the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), plus a larger flow duct in the MSG
investigations.status: Listed as a current combustion experiment by NASA Glenn
investigations.objective: Studies ignition and flammability of solid spacecraft materials in practical geometries and realistic atmospheres, including a microgravity flammability map to compare with the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 worst case.
investigations.fuels: Most likely plastics such as PMMA or Delrin (as planned in the 2015 guide)
investigations.conditions: Chamber oxygen from 10% to 40% by volume at 0.2 to 1.5 atm; air flows in the spacecraft ventilation range of 0 to 30 cm/s
investigations.variables: Material, oxygen concentration, pressure, flow speed, external heating
investigations.measurements: Not yet summarised

flags.solid_materials: Studies ignition and flammability of solid spacecraft materials
flags.habitat_atmosphere: Oxygen from 10% to 40% at 0.2 to 1.5 atm, which includes exploration atmospheres
flags.ventilation_flow: Air flows in the spacecraft ventilation range of 0 to 30 cm/s

quotes.text: ignition and flammability of solid spacecraft materials in practical geometries
some researchers believe is not conservative in low-g

o2_range.label: 10% to 40% O2 at 0.2 to 1.5 atm (planned chamber range)

investigations.name: Flammability Limits At Reduced-g Experiment
investigations.platform: Ground tests (1g and parabolic flights), then flight experiments in the ISS Japanese module Kibo
investigations.hardware: The same hardware as JAXA's 'Solid Combustion' experiment
investigations.status: Listed as a current combustion experiment by NASA Glenn; flight experiments on orbit were expected in 2017 or later
investigations.objective: Develops a way to correlate material flammability limits in normal gravity and microgravity, so microgravity limits can be estimated from ground data, and aims to propose a new standard test method for screening spacecraft materials. International team including JAXA, NASA and ESA, with universities in Japan, the USA and France.
investigations.fuels: Not yet summarised
investigations.conditions: Not yet summarised
investigations.variables: The flow field, studied through a critical Damkohler number (flow time divided by reaction time) for flame extinction
investigations.measurements: Material flammability limits in normal gravity and microgravity, to verify the correlation

flags.solid_materials: Correlates material flammability limits between normal gravity and microgravity
flags.ventilation_flow: Controls the flow field to study a critical Damkohler number for flame extinction

quotes.text: correlate material flammability limits in normal gravity and microgravity
a new fire safety standard test method for screening spacecraft materials

investigations.name: Flammability of Materials on the Moon
investigations.hardware: Not yet summarised
investigations.objective: Burns four solid fuel samples in quiescent habitable atmospheres in actual long-duration lunar gravity: the first combustion experiment on another planetary body.
investigations.fuels: Synergy Pro Navy fabric sheets, 2 x 20 cm exposed, hot-wire ignition, upward burning
investigations.conditions: Four tests at 8.2 psia with 37%, 33%, 29% and 25% oxygen, in lunar gravity
investigations.variables: Oxygen concentration
investigations.measurements: Not yet summarised

flags.partial_gravity: Tests in actual lunar gravity on the Moon
flags.habitat_atmosphere: 8.2 psia with 25% to 37% oxygen, matching planned lunar habitat atmospheres

quotes.text: first-ever combustion experiment to be performed on another planetary body

investigations.name: Lunar-g Combustion Investigation
investigations.platform: Blue Origin New Shepard suborbital capsule, spun to simulate lunar gravity
investigations.hardware: A combustion chamber in a New Shepard payload locker (floor about 41 x 48 cm, about 53 cm tall), developed by NASA Glenn with Voyager Technologies
investigations.status: Flew on 4 Feb 2025; preliminary results presented in Dec 2025
investigations.objective: Tested whether lunar gravity makes fire more hazardous by burning a fabric and a plastic rod in simulated lunar gravity on a spinning suborbital capsule, and showed that this platform can give flammability data at partial gravity.
investigations.fuels: Two samples burned at the same time: a cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabric sheet, burning downward, and a 4-mm-diameter PMMA (acrylic) rod, burning upward
investigations.conditions: Simulated lunar gravity from a steady 11 rpm rotation (effective radius 1.22 m), in air at normal pressure; the burn lasted over two and a half minutes
investigations.variables: Sample and burn direction; chamber oxygen fell as the burns progressed, so a limiting value for extinction can be defined
investigations.measurements: Flame spread and growth from two orthogonal cameras, and chamber oxygen. Preliminary: SIBAL flame-base spread 0.92 mm/s; PMMA rod flame-tip spread 1.5 mm/s; chamber oxygen fell from 20% to 14.3%.

flags.partial_gravity: Burned materials for over 25 seconds in simulated lunar gravity on a spinning capsule
flags.solid_materials: Burned a cotton-fiberglass fabric and a PMMA rod

quotes.text: first-ever, extended-duration (greater than 25 seconds) combustion tests performed in simulated Lunar gravity
might be a more hazardous environment for fire safety

o2_range.label: Air at normal pressure; chamber oxygen fell from 20% to 14.3% during the burns

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
investigations.objective: Measures how well inert-gas suppressants work in microgravity by burning fuel droplets in oxygen-nitrogen mixtures diluted with a second inert gas, and maps flammability limits for fire safety.
investigations.fuels: Heptane and methanol droplets (MDCA handles droplets of 1 to 5 mm)
investigations.conditions: Oxygen mole fraction from 0.10 to 0.50; diluents nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium or xenon
investigations.variables: Oxygen mole fraction, diluent gas, pressure
investigations.measurements: Droplet burning rate, flame extinction, flame radiation, soot concentration and soot temperature

flags.suppression: Quantifies the effectiveness of inert-gas suppressants such as carbon dioxide and helium
flags.habitat_atmosphere: Oxygen mole fractions up to 0.50, beyond Earth air

quotes.text: assess and quantify the effectiveness of inert-gas suppressants in microgravity
the flammability limit is lower in reduced gravity

investigations.earth_application: The heptane and methanol combustion models are building blocks for models of practical fuels such as diesel and jet fuel.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
investigations.hardware: MDCA in the CIR
investigations.objective: Builds on FLEX with a wider range of fuels, including mixtures of pure fuels and real-fuel surrogates, and studies soot formation, slow convective flow effects and droplet interactions.
investigations.fuels: Mixtures of pure fuels and real-fuel surrogates; one image shows ethanol
investigations.conditions: One example test: ethanol burning in 30% oxygen at 2.4 atm
investigations.variables: Fuel mixture, diluent, flow, droplet spacing
investigations.measurements: Not yet summarised

flags.ventilation_flow: Studies slow sub-buoyant convective flow effects

quotes.text: slow sub-buoyant, convective flow effects and droplet-droplet interactions

o2_range.label: Example test: ethanol in 30% O2 at 2.4 atm

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation
investigations.hardware: MDCA in the CIR
investigations.objective: Burns droplets of liquid fuel to study cool flames. FLEX had earlier observed a cool-flame phenomenon after visible flame extinction.
investigations.fuels: Liquid fuel droplets
investigations.conditions: Not yet summarised
investigations.variables: Not yet summarised
investigations.measurements: Not yet summarised

quotes.text: each featured burning droplets of liquid fuel

investigations.name: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
investigations.hardware: ACME modular hardware in the CIR, with a spherical burner
investigations.objective: Creates inside-out flames: the chamber holds nitrogen and a flammable gas, while an oxygen-nitrogen mixture flows out of a spherical burner. These were the highest-oxygen microgravity tests.
investigations.fuels: A flammable gas such as propane in the chamber
investigations.conditions: Oxygen-nitrogen mixture of up to 85% oxygen from the burner
investigations.variables: Not yet summarised
investigations.measurements: Not yet summarised

flags.habitat_atmosphere: The highest oxygen concentrations of the microgravity tests, up to 85% oxygen

quotes.text: an oxygen-nitrogen mixture of up to 85% oxygen flowed from the spherical burner

o2_range.label: Up to 85% O2 flowing from the burner

investigations.name: Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.hardware: ACME modular hardware in the CIR, with a flat porous burner
investigations.objective: Emulates the burning of solid and liquid fuels with a gas-fed porous burner whose fuel flow follows the measured heat flux, to study materials flammability and test how well current flammability tests apply in low and partial gravity.
investigations.fuels: Gaseous fuels chosen to simulate fuels such as paper, plastic and alcohol
investigations.conditions: Still (quiescent) atmospheres
investigations.variables: Emulated material properties, fuel flow rate
investigations.measurements: Heat flux at the burner and surface temperature (used to control the fuel flow)

flags.solid_materials: Studies materials flammability, such as ignition and extinction, by emulating solid fuels
flags.partial_gravity: Assesses whether existing flammability test methods apply in low and partial gravity

quotes.text: assess the relevance of existing flammability test methods for low- and partial-gravity environments

investigations.name: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
investigations.hardware: ACME modular hardware in the CIR; a high-voltage field (up to 10 kV) between the burner and a mesh above it
investigations.objective: Studies how electric fields act on the ions in flames and how they can be used to control flames. Because the field pushes on the ions, it was used to mimic partial gravity.
investigations.fuels: Gas-jet or coflow diffusion flames
investigations.conditions: Electric field up to 10 kV
investigations.variables: Field strength, fuel dilution
investigations.measurements: Ion current through the flame and the flame's response time to electric forcing

flags.partial_gravity: Mimicked partial gravity through the effect of the electric field on flame ions

quotes.text: Partial gravity was mimicked in ACME’s Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames

investigations.name: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
investigations.hardware: ACME modular hardware in the CIR
investigations.objective: Extends the range of flame conditions that can be predicted accurately by testing chemical kinetic and soot models on very dilute and very sooty lifted flames.
investigations.fuels: Diluted methane and ethylene in an air coflow
investigations.conditions: Not yet summarised
investigations.variables: Injection velocity, fuel dilution
investigations.measurements: Flame structure

quotes.text: extend the range of flame conditions that can be accurately predicted

investigations.earth_application: Applicable to practical combustion issues such as turbulent combustion, ignition and flame stability.

investigations.name: Flame Design
investigations.hardware: ACME modular hardware in the CIR, with a porous spherical burner
investigations.objective: Studies soot inception and control so that oxygen-enriched combustion can be optimised and flames can be designed to be robust and soot-free.
investigations.fuels: Ethylene or methane
investigations.conditions: Oxygen-enriched atmospheres (concentrations varied)
investigations.variables: Fuel concentration, oxygen concentration, flow direction
investigations.measurements: Soot inception and extinction limits

quotes.text: improve our understanding of soot inception and control

investigations.earth_application: Could lead to burner designs that are more efficient and less polluting.

investigations.name: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
investigations.hardware: ACME modular hardware in the CIR, with a porous spherical burner
investigations.objective: Uses spherical flames, possible only in microgravity, to predict the structure and dynamics of flames, including extinction.
investigations.fuels: Hydrogen and methane (soot-free flames) and ethylene (sooty flames)
investigations.conditions: Various inert diluents in the fuel and in the chamber
investigations.variables: Fuel, diluent
investigations.measurements: Extinction limits; onset of pulsating instabilities

quotes.text: predict the structure and dynamics, including extinction, of both soot-free and sooty flames

investigations.name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
investigations.hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with a fan-driven flow duct, later reused by BASS and SLICE
investigations.objective: Finds the point at which gas-jet flames start to emit soot in microgravity, for several fuels and nozzle and co-flow settings.
investigations.fuels: Several gaseous fuels
investigations.conditions: Different nozzle diameter and co-flow velocity configurations
investigations.variables: Fuel, nozzle diameter, co-flow velocity
investigations.measurements: Smoke point, flame shape, flame stabilisation height and temperature field

flags.ventilation_flow: Varies the co-flow velocity around the flame

quotes.text: laminar smoke point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames
improved flammability criteria for selection of materials

investigations.earth_application: Supports improved design of practical combustors through better control of soot formation.

investigations.name: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
investigations.hardware: SPICE hardware in the MSG
investigations.objective: Studies the structure of lifting and lifted flames, where the flame detaches from the burner, to test and improve combustion models. A precursor to the CLD Flame experiment.
investigations.fuels: Methane, ethylene and nitrogen dilutions of each, in a co-flow of air
investigations.conditions: Air co-flow at varied velocity
investigations.variables: Fuel, burner diameter, flow conditions
investigations.measurements: Flame structure from attached to lifted conditions; liftoff velocity limits

quotes.text: structure of lifting and lifted flames

investigations.earth_application: Aims at higher fuel efficiency and lower pollutant emission in practical combustion devices.

investigations.name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
investigations.hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), Expedition 15
investigations.status: Conducted in the MSG during ISS Expedition 15
investigations.objective: Measures the size distribution of smoke particles from spacecraft materials and evaluates the ionization (Shuttle) and photoelectric (ISS) smoke detectors in microgravity.
investigations.fuels: 30 samples: six each of Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, cellulose and dibutyl phthalate on a porous wick
investigations.conditions: Different air flow rates, heating temperatures and smoke aging durations
investigations.variables: Material, air flow rate, heating temperature, smoke aging time
investigations.measurements: Smoke particle size distribution and relative abundance

flags.detection: Evaluates spacecraft smoke detectors and measures smoke particle sizes

quotes.text: assess the size and distribution of smoke particles produced by different types of material

investigations.earth_application: Smoke detectors developed from SAME results can be useful in other extreme environments on Earth, such as submarines or underwater laboratories.

investigations.name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment reflight (SAME-R, also called SAME-2)
investigations.hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)
investigations.status: Conducted on ISS Expedition 24 (July to September 2010)
investigations.objective: A reflight of SAME that added diagnostics and expanded the test matrix, to measure smoke from spacecraft materials well enough to improve the design of future smoke detectors.
investigations.fuels: Five materials representative of spacecraft: Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone rubber and Pyrell, heated below their ignition point
investigations.conditions: Air flow past the sample from quiescent to 8 cm/s; smoke held in an aging chamber for 11 to 1800 s before measurement
investigations.variables: Material, sample surface temperature, air flow, smoke aging time
investigations.measurements: Particle number, diameter and mass concentrations, a prototype two-moment smoke detector, and TEM grids for particle shape and size. Most average particle sizes were 200 to 400 nm.

flags.detection: Measured smoke particle sizes from spacecraft materials and tested a prototype smoke detector

quotes.text: measurements of smoke from spacecraft fires to enable improved design of future detectors

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.hardware: A modified P-Trak ultrafine particle counter, operable almost anywhere in the ISS
investigations.objective: Measured background dust and particle levels on the ISS and checked that the P-Trak counter later used by SAME works in microgravity.
investigations.fuels: None: background particulate in the ISS cabin
investigations.conditions: ISS cabin air
investigations.variables: Location in the ISS, particle size range
investigations.measurements: Ultrafine particle counts across the ISS (SAME requires counts of particles from 0.2 to 1 micron)

flags.detection: Characterises background dust so detectors can tell dust from smoke

quotes.text: help design better smoke detectors capable of distinguishing normal dust from dangerous smoke particles

investigations.earth_application: Smoke detectors developed from SAME results can be useful in submarines or underwater laboratories.

investigations.name: Water Mist Fire Suppression experiment
investigations.hardware: Combustion Module (CM) facility
investigations.objective: Measured how water droplet size and water concentration affect the speed, strength and shape of flames, to design better water-mist fire suppression to replace Halon systems.
investigations.fuels: Premixed flames in various fuel and oxygen mixtures
investigations.conditions: Not yet summarised
investigations.variables: Water droplet diameter, water concentration, fuel-oxygen mixture
investigations.measurements: Flame speed, strength and shape

quotes.text: water-mist portable fire extinguishers were designed, tested, fabricated and certified for spaceflight

investigations.earth_application: Fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for the ISS have practical applications on Earth.

earth_applications.title: Water-mist fire extinguishers
earth_applications.text: Fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for use on the ISS have practical applications on Earth. The first two ISS units were sent in December 2015 to replace carbon dioxide extinguishers.

earth_applications.title: Smoke detectors for extreme environments
earth_applications.text: Smoke detectors developed from SAME results can be useful on Earth in submarines or underwater laboratories.

earth_applications.title: Fewer nuisance alarms
earth_applications.text: A 1970s smoke detector developed for the Shuttle tells smoke from dust, giving fewer nuisance alarms; it has industrial uses such as mining.
earth_applications.location: Described on the challenge Resources tab

earth_applications.title: Firefighter air tanks
earth_applications.text: In the 1970s, spacesuit technology was adapted to improve firefighters' air tanks and breathing gear.
earth_applications.location: Described on the challenge Resources tab

earth_applications.title: Firefighter clothing
earth_applications.text: In the 1980s, NASA spacesuit technology was applied to improve firefighter clothing.
earth_applications.location: Described on the challenge Resources tab

earth_applications.title: Models for diesel and jet fuel
earth_applications.text: FLEX's heptane and methanol combustion models are building blocks for models of practical liquid fuels such as diesel and jet fuel.

earth_applications.title: Fire models on Earth
earth_applications.text: BASS results feed combustion models used in designing fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth.
